result.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
result.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Accepted at the WAM-AD Workshop, WACV 2027. Code: https://github.com/binayksingh/does-action-matter
result.summary: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action. In this paper, we study action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action. We compare a forecaster with feature-wise and input-level action conditioning against an identical model without action input, and measure action dependence with test-time action interventions scored by standard segmentation metrics. The evaluation is validated in a synthetic environment with known action-dependent dynamics and applied to Cityscapes and BDD100K, both within each dataset and across the two vehicle platforms. Experiments show that the executed action improves mid-term mIoU by at most 2.5 points on Cityscapes and 0.6 points on BDD100K, whereas a wrong action reduces it by up to 23.2 and 7.0 points, below the model without action input. On real data, feature-wise conditioning depends 1.6 times more on the action than input-level conditioning at similar accuracy, whereas both depend on it equally in the synthetic environment, where the history does not determine the action. These results show that an accuracy gain indicates that a driving world model uses its action, but not how strongly its forecasts depend on it. Code is available at https://github.com/binayksingh/does-action-matter.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究动作条件语义预测（由历史语义分割与自车动作预测未来分割）是否真正依赖动作输入：将带动作条件的模型与结构相同但无动作输入的模型对比，并在测试时干预动作、用分割指标量化依赖程度，在合成环境、Cityscapes 和 BDD100K 上评估，发现正确动作只带来小幅 mIoU 增益，而错误动作会造成远大于此的下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「测试时干预条件输入并量化输出依赖」的范式可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正使用视觉证据、动作或中间推理内容，以及贡献分配是否虚假；但该工作属驾驶世界模型、不含 VLM 推理轨迹，指标与结论能否迁移需阅读原文判断。
